transcript:
Meeting Header: Recorded at 2026-07-09T15:00:00-07:00, Duration 42 minutes. Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ben Ortega (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Quartz CTO), Priya Rao (Head of Product), Marco Diaz (SRE).

Summary: Quick renewal check-in; customer is leaning toward dedicated reserved capacity for cost predictability and wants EU + APAC regions; requested benchmarks and SOC2/ISO documents.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. We're here to talk through your renewal, the capacity upgrade you mentioned, and the region add - quick round-robin intros?
[00:22] Alex: Yep, Alex Chen, CTO at Quartz. We're mainly focused on latency and cost, want to make sure the new plan covers EU data residency for some clients.
[00:30] Priya: Priya Rao, head of product - I'll be owning rollout and success metrics.
[00:36] Marco: Marco Diaz, SRE - I'll help with benchmarks and infra.
[00:40] Ben: Ben Ortega, Redwood SE - I'll drive the benchmark plan and technical details.

[02:15] Maya: Great. Quick context from our side - your current contract renews 2026-08-01, you're on a hosted plan with about 4-GPU equivalent steady usage and some burst. You flagged needing more predictable throughput and multi-region. Is that right?
[02:35] Alex: Yeah, that's accurate. We're seeing growth in EU customers and some enterprise deals want EU-only processing. Also had a pilot in APAC that we want to support soon. Cost predictability really matters for our finance team.
[03:12] Priya: For success criteria we need p95 generation latency under 350ms for typical requests and token cost within our current % budget. Also, availability SLOs for our endpoints.

[04:00] Ben: Understood - for the latency target, we recommend a dedicated pool. With 10 GPUs pinned you should see consistent p95s; exact numbers depend on model and quantization. We'll run a workload-specific benchmark.
[04:30] Marco: Quick question - how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? We saw some doc saying K-V cash - sorry, that was from earlier notes. But basically we need cache behavior to persist across requests for our chat flows.
[04:52] Ben: Yep, Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching; we'll map your session keys and we can show cache hit rates in the console. There might be some name munging in auto transcripts but function is there.

[07:10] Alex: On regions: what's the timeline to spin up an EU region and APAC? We need to understand lead time and price uplift.
[07:25] Maya: EU can be added as part of the Dedicated plan fairly quickly - we typically provision within 2-3 weeks after sign-off for a reserved pool. APAC is a bit longer depending on capacity, usually 4-6 weeks. Pricing will include region add-ons; I'll get you exact numbers in the quote.
[08:00] Priya: For compliance, can you confirm SOC2, ISO, and KMS options? We need to show auditors.
[08:12] Maya: Yes - SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are available. We support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments; for Dedicated we offer tenant-level encryption keys on request. I'll share the certs and a network diagram.
[08:40] Marco: And SSO? We use Okta, SAML.
[08:45] Ben: We support SAML/SSO and RBAC roles at the project level. Minor caveat: some older console features require a role mapping step.

[12:30] Alex: Pricing - we ran a rough model comparing Redwood dedicated vs self-hosting; Redwood looks cleaner operationally but we need to validate per-token costs at scale. Any levers to reduce token spend?
[12:50] Ben: Yes - batching, quantization (int8/4bit where appropriate), and automatic prefix caching are primary levers. Redwood Optimize will recommend quant profiles per model. Also, routing lower-critical traffic to cheaper model variants helps.
[13:20] Priya: If we add more GPUs, how does autoscaling/burst work? We don't want to be billed for idle GPUs but need burst when cadence spikes.
[13:34] Maya: With Dedicated you can configure a reserved base and burst pool; we can set policies so you only pay for burst when used. We'll include recommended autoscale settings in the proposal.

[18:00] Ben: For the benchmark plan - propose we run two tests: 1) EU region steady-state with your production traffic sample, measuring p50/p95/p99 and token cost; 2) Mixed-region failover test to validate graceful degradation. Marco, can you provide traffic traces and SLOs?
[18:20] Marco: Yes, I'll upload traces and a short script to replay. ETA Tuesday.
[18:35] Ben: Perfect - we'll provision a 10-GPU pool mirror in EU for the run. Note: depending on the model we pick, kernel selection may change latency; we'll document which kernels and quant settings we used.

[25:00] Alex: Contract term - we're considering a 12 vs 24 month extension. Any discounts for longer commitments?
[25:15] Maya: Yes, we have stepped discounts for 12 vs 24 month reserved capacity. For a 24-month commit on a dedicated pool we can offer additional pricing credits; I'll include tiered options in the quote.
[25:45] Priya: We also need an addendum for data residency and audit access.
[25:50] Maya: Noted - legal will draft an addendum that includes region residency and audit log access.

[32:00] Alex: One more technical: when capacity is constrained do you have automatic fallbacks to hosted models in other regions? We need graceful degradation.
[32:12] Ben: Yes, routing policies can failover to compatible model variants or hosted capacity with automatic throttling. You can define policy by latency or cost. We'll demo that in the follow-up.
[32:45] Marco: Important that fallback don't send data to regions we flagged as restricted. Can RBAC/policy prevent that?
[33:00] Ben: Absolutely - region/tenant binding and routing rules can ensure restricted data never leaves allowed regions. We'll include a config example.

[38:00] Priya: Ok, recap would be great - benchmarks, pricing, SOC2 docs, addendum, and next steps to finalize by mid-July so procurement can sign before Aug 1.
[38:18] Maya: Yep. Action items: I'll send pricing and SOC2/ISO docs by Fri (2026-07-10). Ben will schedule EU benchmark with Marco for 2026-07-16. Legal & I will draft the extension addendum by 2026-07-20.
[38:50] Alex: Sounds good. One small note - we mentioned Anthropic and Cohere as alternatives during vendor review; we'll share our evaluation matrix later.

[41:00] Maya: Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and book the benchmark slot.
[41:12] Alex: Thanks, talk soon.

End of meeting.
